Evidence: political lobbying, ideological lesson plans, charter review

Senate Republicans released a report criticizing the NEA's $670 million political spend and partnerships with radical education groups, pushing to revoke its federal charter.

Shining a light on political spending in public education forces transparency on how member dues are allocated.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing institutional oversight with partisan retaliation (WHO vs WHAT).

The bait-and-switch frames union reform as student protection.

Social Physics Analysis:
Instead of addressing root educational challenges transparently, leaders project partisan blame. This maintains a perpetual conflict loop for political leverage rather than solving strain.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
It plots toward Lesser Evil because partisan posturing replaces genuine educational reform with institutional warfare.

Mathematical divergence yields negative social alignment.

The Unavoidable Truth: Public unions spend hundreds of millions on partisan political advocacy.

The Unavoidable Lie: Revoking a federal charter solves classroom reading scores.
